title: ieee80211: update code to final 802.11be amendment
description:
The changes are the following:
* Add missing new status code
* Remove amendment and draft indications
* Update EML Capabilities subfield to final format
* Renaming of some field to match their name in the standard

This is definitely not an exhaustive update; more change might be needed

notes.body: This looks good in my review

added 1 commit
  • 7a02c386 - ieee80211: update code to final 802.11be amendment
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23352/diffs?diff_id=1638392749&start_sha=30b595cbe7178613629cc1e1d0ef9b41fd561cc8)
added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 2

[Is this an issue with decoding the 802.11be management frame ETH PHY Bits 64-71?](https://ask.wireshark.org/question/37890/is-this-an-issue-with-decoding-the-80211be-management-frame-eth-phy-bits-64-71/)  
  
There is a bug fix in this merge that should be cherry picked back 4.6 ?  
```
    {&hf_ieee80211_eht_phy_bits_64_71,
     {"EHT PHY Bits 64-71", "wlan.eht.phy_capabilities.bits_64_71",
-     FT_UINT24, BASE_HEX, NULL, 0x0, NULL, HFILL }},
+     FT_UINT8, BASE_HEX, NULL, 0x0, NULL, HFILL }},
```

> There is a bug fix in this merge that should be cherry picked back 4.6 ?

Anything that causes problems dissecting frames that match the final standard, with the possible exception of fields not being dissected at all, should probably be backported.
I'm not sure the whole commit is a bug fix vs a chunk of it being updates/enhancements?

> I'm not sure the whole commit is a bug fix vs a chunk of it being updates/enhancements?

That's what "with the possible exception of fields not being dissected at all" is about - if something is dissected *incorrectly* for frames matching the final standard, that should be backported, but cases where the field wasn't dissected at all (i.e., skipped over or dissected as an opaque blob), maybe not.

I would probably recommend extracting this one line fix over cherry-picking the whole commit. It's mainly some renaming of field to match more closely to the standard, some typo fixes, the removal of draft mention, not really worth the backporting.
